leah_p: quick thread — dedicated roadmap milestone: decide autoscale prewarm vs sustained-headroom default for reserved pools.
omar_s: context: several mid-market customers want predictable latency during burst windows. two asks: 1) guaranteed small sustained headroom always-on (costly), 2) prewarm on predicted surge (cheaper but riskier).
tess: summary of tradeoffs:
- sustained-headroom: predictable perf, higher baseline cost, simpler billing
- predictive-prewarm: lower avg cost, requires good signals + scheduling, risk of misprediction
akio: we tried simple ML predictor in Q4; precision was ok for big events but noisy for small spikes. ops overhead to manage false positives was nontrivial.
leah_p: customer-driven constraint: Enterprise legal wants explicit SLA language about burst availability for some contracts.
omar_s: proposal: default = predictive-prewarm with a paid optional add-on for sustained-headroom. make onboarding checklist highlight SLA differences.
tess: spec bullets for defaults page:
- default pool mode: predictive-prewarm (opt-in sustained-headroom add-on)
- SLA tiers: standard (best-effort burst), guaranteed (sustained-headroom)
- pricing: sustained add-on billed as monthly reserve + small per-use delta
product-bot: checklist created: docs + sales playbook + metrics for pilot.
leah_p: launch criteria for pilot: 3 customers signed for add-on, 99.5% burst-availability in canary, latency regressions <5%.
omar_s: implementation plan: 1) enable predictor + prewarm hooks in runtime 2) build add-on billing 3) create sales collateral
tess: risks: gating the add-on might slow adoption; predictive model improvements needed. ops: need runbook for missed prewarms -> fall back to best-effort with customer notice.
akio: timeline ask: can we pilot predictive default + one sustained-headroom customer in 6 weeks?
leah_p: optimistic but OK. assign owners: omar=eng delivery, tess=sales doc, akio=ops runbook. update in weekly roadmap review.
leah_p: adding action items in product tracker now.
